topic: Separating Mixtures by Winnowing, Scooping, Evaporation, and Magnets
key_concepts: Winnowing uses moving air to carry away lighter husks while heavier rice grains remain.
Scooping can remove a floating oil layer from water.
Oil floats on water because it is less dense.
Evaporation separates a dissolved solid like salt from water by heating.
Salt remains in the evaporating dish after water evaporates.
Magnets attract iron filings but not sand.
A magnet can be used to separate iron filings from a sand mixture.
